D has the smallest total, 9, so it is the barycenter, in the accent color; the card returns its id 4. The center, which minimizes the farthest distance instead, is E, one step down the tail." width="100%"} The barycenter (or *median*) of a graph is the set of nodes whose sum of shortest-path distances to every other node is smallest. Where `center()` minimizes the worst-case distance, the barycenter minimizes the average: it is the best place for a facility when every trip counts, not just the longest one. The two can differ when the graph is lopsided, since many nearby nodes pull the barycenter toward them. Distances follow the same rule as `shortest_path()`: total edge weight on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`), hop count otherwise, unless `weighted=` says otherwise. On a directed graph they follow edge direction. Total distance is only finite when every node can reach every other, so the graph must be connected (strongly connected if directed). The minimum total itself is the closeness denominator: the barycenter nodes are exactly those with the highest `closeness_centrality()` on a connected graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure distances by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Edges without a weight count as `1.0`; weights must be non-negative. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted IDs of the barycenter nodes. Empty for an empty graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not connected (not strongly connected, if directed), or weights are used and one is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A star with a long tail: the tail end G is far from everything, so the center (which minimizes the worst case) shifts down the tail, while the barycenter (which minimizes the total) stays at the hub, close to the many leaves: ::: {#552d31b3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["hub", "A", "B", "C", "X", "D", "E", "F", "G"]) .add_edges([("hub", "A"), ("hub", "B"), ("hub", "C"), ("hub", "X"), ("hub", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "G")]) ) label = graph.get_label_from_id [label(n) for n in graph.center()], [label(n) for n in graph.barycenter()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['D', 'E'], ['hub']) ``` ::: :::
